instructions: Heat the oven to 450°F with one rack in the lower third and one in the upper third.
Whisk the chickpea flour, 1 3/4 cups water, 2 tbsp of the oil and 1 tsp salt in a bowl until there are no lumps. Leave it on the counter.
Cut the zucchini into 1/2 inch half-moons. Cut the peppers into 1 inch pieces, the onion into wedges and the mushrooms in half. Toss them on a rimmed baking sheet with 3 tbsp oil and 1/2 tsp salt.
Put the vegetables on the lower rack. Pour 2 tbsp oil onto a second rimmed baking sheet, tilt it to coat, and put it on the upper rack.
After 5 minutes, pull the upper rack out partway. Whisk the batter again and pour it onto the hot sheet. Push the rack back in.
Five minutes later, stir the vegetables. Bake everything for 10 minutes, until the socca is set with brown edges and the vegetables are browned.
Chop the basil and cut the lemon in half.
Take both sheets out. Cut the socca into squares. Squeeze the lemon over the vegetables and toss in most of the basil.
Taste the vegetables. If they're flat, add a pinch more salt.
Serve the socca squares topped with the vegetables and the rest of the basil, drizzled with the last 1 tbsp oil, with the red pepper flakes on the table.
method_notes: The sources agree on a batter of chickpea flour, water, salt and olive oil that rests before it goes into a very hot oiled pan, and a topping of roasted vegetables. They differ on the cooking method (oven at 350°F, under the broiler, or thin pancakes on the stove), on the rest (30 minutes to an hour) and on the vegetables. To fit 45 minutes this bakes one sheet-pan socca at 450°F while the vegetables roast, rests the batter only as long as it takes to chop, and uses 1 3/4 cups water to 1 1/2 cups flour. It is naturally vegan and gluten-free.
